userStories.title: Run memory switch
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the default-on memory.inRun configuration switch without changing chat behavior.

**Motivation** — A `nax run` starts every story blank.

**Approach** — Config (`memory.inRun`)

```jsonc
"memory": {
  "enabled": true,
  "provider": "local",
  "writeMode": "direct",
  "indexBytes": 24576,
  "askOnSave": true,
  "inRun": true            // false: nax run gets no memory sync, index or tools; chat is unaffected
}
```

`MemoryConfigSchema` gains `inRun: z.boolean().default(true)`; it stays `.strict()`, so `stages` and `koda` remain unknown keys. `MemoryConfig` (`src/config/runtime-types-memory.ts`) gains `inRun: boolean`. `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` gains `memory.inRun`. `memory.enabled: false` still turns everything off (step 2 above).

`packages/nax/test/unit/config/schemas-memory.test.ts` — `DEFAULT_MEMORY` and the AC-9 `configured` literal are closed `toEqual` objects of the memory block; both gain `inRun` (`true` in the default, `false` in the configured literal), and the invariant stays "the parsed default and a configured block round-trip exactly".

**Scope** — In: schemas-memory.ts, runtime-types-memory.ts, cli/config-descriptions.ts and the existing schema tests, including complete MemoryConfig fixture compatibility. Out: createRunMemory and switch consumption (US-003), prompt rendering (US-002), runtime/setup wiring (US-005/US-006). The design's memory.stages list is not built.

**Interface** — Exact field declarations to add:
```ts
inRun: z.boolean().default(true)
inRun: boolean
```
The first is the MemoryConfigSchema object entry; the second is the MemoryConfig member. Use memoryConfigOf rather than adding independent defaults.

Verification note: `bun run typecheck` passes with `MemoryConfig.inRun` declared. Write failing tests in test/unit/config/schemas-memory.test.ts before implementation; preserve the closed default and configured equality assertions, not partial matches.
acceptanceCriteria: NaxConfigSchema.parse({}).memory.inRun is true.
NaxConfigSchema.parse({ memory: { inRun: false } }).memory.inRun is false.
NaxConfigSchema.safeParse({ memory: { inRun: "yes" } }) fails with an issue whose path is ["memory", "inRun"].
NaxConfigSchema.safeParse({ memory: { stages: ["run"] } }) still fails because memory accepts no unknown key.
memoryConfigOf({}).inRun is true.
FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS["memory.inRun"] is a non-empty string.

routing.reasoning: Small additive Zod/runtime-type/description change across three source files, with exact-default fixture compatibility and no permission-policy changes.

`DEFAULT_MEMORY` and the AC-9 `configured` literal are closed `toEqual` objects of the memory block; both gain `inRun` (`true` in the default, `false` in the configured literal), and the invariant stays "the parsed default and a configured block round-trip exactly".

userStories.title: Memory sections in workflow prompts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add optional memory sections to the implementer brief, branch fix, CI repair and whole-branch review builders.

**Motivation** — What an earlier chat or run worked out (a test command that needs a container, a review ruling, a reason a fix was reverted) is in the memory mirror, but no run session sees it, and a run session cannot save what the next one would need.

**Approach** — Prompt builders

`src/prompts/builders/memory-builder.ts` gains:

```ts
/** The read-only memory section: the index as background, for a session without the memory tools. */
export function buildMemoryReferenceSection(memoryIndex: string): string;
export function memoryReferenceSectionOf(memoryIndex: string | undefined): string | undefined;
```

`buildMemoryReferenceSection(index)` returns `"## Memory\n\n" + MEMORY_REFERENCE_NOTE + "\n\n" + index`, where `MEMORY_REFERENCE_NOTE` is `"Notes earlier sessions saved for this project, one line each. Use them as background; you cannot read or change them in this session."`. `memoryReferenceSectionOf` returns `undefined` for an `undefined` or `""` index, like the existing `memorySectionOf`. Both are exported from `src/prompts/index.ts`.

Each builder below gains an optional `memoryIndex?: string` input. Absent or `""`, its output is byte-identical to today's.

| Builder | File | Section | Placement |
|---|---|---|---|
| `buildWorkflowBrief` | `workflow-implementer-builder.ts` | `memorySectionOf` (tool section) | after the `## Rules index` section (when present) and before `## Feature context` |
| `buildWorkflowBranchFixPrompt` | `workflow-branch-builder.ts` | `memorySectionOf` | after the `## How to work` list, before `WORKFLOW_REPLY_CONTRACT` |
| `buildWorkflowCiRepairPrompt` | `workflow-ci-repair-builder.ts` | `memorySectionOf` | after `REPAIR_VERIFICATION_RULE`, before `WORKFLOW_REPLY_CONTRACT` |
| `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt` | `workflow-branch-builder.ts` (`BranchReviewPromptInput`) | `memoryReferenceSectionOf` | before the `## Your remit` heading |

Changed (the baseline exists only to locate the code; the target is the interface to implement):
- `buildWorkflowBrief(input: WorkflowBriefInput)`. Target: `WorkflowBriefInput` gains `memoryIndex?: string`.
- `buildWorkflowBranchFixPrompt(input: { specPath?; prdPath?; reportPath; findings })`. Target: the input gains `memoryIndex?: string`.
- `buildWorkflowCiRepairPrompt(input: { round; prUrl?; specPath?; prdPath?; reportPath; findings })`. Target: the input gains `readonly memoryIndex?: string`.
- `BranchReviewPromptInput`. Target: gains `readonly memoryIndex?: string`.

`src/prompts/index.ts` — export `buildMemoryReferenceSection`, `memoryReferenceSectionOf` and `memorySectionOf`.

**Scope** — In: memory-builder.ts, prompts/index.ts, workflow-implementer-builder.ts, workflow-branch-builder.ts, workflow-ci-repair-builder.ts and existing prompt/brief-order tests. Out: acquiring or syncing memory (US-003/US-004), provider attachment (US-005), and reading runtime.memory at callers (US-007). Story re-reviews, branch re-reviews and the advisor get no memory section. Review-stage sessions get no read-only memory tools; the whole-branch reviewer sees only index lines. The story reviewer keeps reading the implementer's brief without its own prompt/tool changes.

**Interface** — The new helper signatures above are final. Preserve the existing `memorySectionOf(memoryIndex: string | undefined): string | undefined` behavior and existing builder signatures except for the specified optional memoryIndex fields. These builders remain pure: no memory hosts, config reads, filesystem reads or model calls.

Testing: extend test/unit/prompts/builders/memory-builder.test.ts and the existing workflow builder tests, and use test/unit/workflow/brief-rules-index.test.ts for section-order regression anchors. Compare no-index and empty-index outputs against existing output, not just absence of a heading.

userStories.title: Runtime carries and closes run memory
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry optional RunMemory through NaxRuntime, advertise its provider after existing providers and guarantee its close on runtime teardown.

**Motivation** — Feature 2 made memory real for `nax chat`; this feature makes the same notes visible, and writable, in the sessions that do a run's work.

**Approach** — Runtime

`NaxRuntime` (`src/runtime/index.ts`) gains `readonly memory?: RunMemory` and `CreateRuntimeOptions` gains `memory?: RunMemory` (`import type { RunMemory } from "../memory"`, matching the file's relative imports, so the runtime adds no runtime import edge). `createRuntime`:

- appends `opts.memory.provider` after the existing providers (MCP, then skills) when `opts.memory` is set; the list is unchanged otherwise;
- returns `memory: opts.memory` only when it is set (no `memory` key otherwise);
- in `close()`, awaits `opts.memory.close()` once (the existing `closed` guard already makes `close()` idempotent), in a `finally` around the rest of the close body, so a rejection from `mcpPool.close()` or a flush cannot skip the run-end sync; `memory.close()` never throws.

`src/runtime/index.ts` is at 597 of 600 lines. To make room, `CreateRuntimeOptions` moves verbatim (with its doc comments) into a new `src/runtime/runtime-options.ts`, and `index.ts` re-exports it (`export type { CreateRuntimeOptions } from "./runtime-options"`), so every importer is unchanged. The move is a precondition of the line cap, not a behaviour change, and is checked by `bun run typecheck` and `bun run check:file-sizes`.

Changed (the baseline exists only to locate the code; the target is the interface to implement):
- `CreateRuntimeOptions`. Baseline: declared in `src/runtime/index.ts:294`. Target: declared in `src/runtime/runtime-options.ts`, re-exported from `src/runtime/index.ts`, with one more optional field `memory?: RunMemory`.
- `NaxRuntime`. Target: gains `readonly memory?: RunMemory`.

Integration: US-004 `RunMemory.provider` / `close` → US-005 `createRuntime`: entry point `createRuntime(config, workdir, { memory })`, observed through `runtime.toolProviders` and `runtime.close()`. `src/runtime/run-tool-providers.ts` — `withRunSkills`. Existing operations already forward runtime providers with each op's pipelineStage; no new role list or dispatch wiring is needed.

**Scope** — In: move the options interface verbatim with its comments to runtime-options.ts, add the optional memory fields using type-only imports, append the provider, conditionally expose memory and close it in finally; create runtime-memory.test.ts. Out: constructing memory in setup (US-006), composing memory/counters (US-003/US-004), prompt rendering and callers (US-002/US-007). Bot review, bot fix and plan entry points must continue creating runtimes without a run memory; do not enable memory in those commands. No permission-policy changes, read-only review tools or packages/nax-agent edits.

**Interface** — Exact existing factory signature retained:
```ts
export function createRuntime(config: NaxConfig, workdir: string, opts?: CreateRuntimeOptions): NaxRuntime
```
Exact added members and re-export:
```ts
// NaxRuntime
readonly memory?: RunMemory;
// CreateRuntimeOptions
memory?: RunMemory;
export type { CreateRuntimeOptions } from "./runtime-options";
```
Both modules use `import type { RunMemory } from "../memory"`. Keep all prior options and their doc comments, including parentSignal, sessionManager, agentManager, costAggregator, promptAuditor, usageAuditor, reviewAuditor, featureName, pidRegistry, dryRun, agentStreamEvents and commandInterceptor.

Testing: model provider-order cases on runtime-skills-provider.test.ts and invoke the real createRuntime with a fake RunMemory. Assert missing property versus undefined, MCP/skills/memory order, unchanged no-memory ids, once-only awaited close and finally execution after MCP close rejection. Preserve rejection of the original runtime teardown error; only memory's own sync failure is nonfatal under its contract. Run typecheck, file-size and import-cycle verification as gates, not new acceptance criteria.

userStories.title: Run setup creates workflow memory
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create run memory once during non-dry workflow setup and pass it to the runtime after resolving runtime configuration.

**Motivation** — A `nax run` starts every story blank.

**Approach** — Run setup

`setupRun` (`src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts`, 557 lines) first resolves the runtime config into a local (today `runtimeConfigFor(config, workdir)` is evaluated inline as the first argument of `createRuntime`, `run-setup.ts:263`), then creates the run memory, then calls `createRuntime` with that local, so a throwing `runtimeConfigFor` never leaves a created run memory unclosed (a synchronous throw from `createRuntime` itself still would, the same gap the runtime's own resources have; the mirror holds nothing that needs closing). The run memory is created when, and only when, `isWorkflowMode(config)` is true and `options.dryRun` is false:

```ts
const runtimeConfig = await runtimeConfigFor(config, workdir);
const memory =
  !options.dryRun && isWorkflowMode(config)
    ? await _runSetupDeps.createRunMemory({ config, repoRoot: workdir, logger: getLogger() })
    : undefined;
```

and passes `...(memory ? { memory } : {})` in the `createRuntime(runtimeConfig, workdir, …)` options. `_runSetupDeps` gains `createRunMemory`; `run-setup.ts` gains imports of `getLogger` (`@/logger`) and `isWorkflowMode` (`@/config`). The CLI initialises the run logger (`bin/nax.ts`) before `setupRun`, so the logger captured here is the run's. `createRunMemory` never throws, so this adds no failure path to setup. The run end is `runtime.close()`, which `runner.ts` awaits in the innermost `finally` on every exit path, and which `setupRun`'s own failure cleanup (`run-setup.ts:548`) also calls.

Test impact: the default `execution.mode` is workflow, so every test that drives the real `setupRun` with `dryRun: false` would now run the real `createRunMemory`. `test/preload.ts` points `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` at an isolated directory, so no test touches the real `~/.nax`, but the lifecycle unit tests that replace `_runSetupDeps.createRuntime` are authorised (US-006 Modifies) to replace `_runSetupDeps.createRunMemory` with one resolving `undefined` in the same fixture. The runner-level integration and e2e tests keep the real run memory: it runs against the isolated directory exactly as a real run would, and adds one `Memory: 0 saved (0 pending)` info line.

Authorized fixture modifications (all under packages/nax/test/unit/execution/lifecycle): gitignore-reconcile.test.ts; run-setup-approvals-seal.test.ts; run-setup-chat-asks.test.ts; run-setup-command-interceptor.test.ts; run-setup-locks.test.ts; run-setup-mcp-in-run.test.ts; run-setup-no-migration.test.ts; run-setup-warnings-native-defaults.test.ts; run-setup-warnings.test.ts; run-setup.test.ts; scratchpad-wipe.test.ts. Each fixture replaces _runSetupDeps.createRuntime and drives the real setupRun in workflow mode, which now also calls real createRunMemory; the fixture may replace _runSetupDeps.createRunMemory with one resolving undefined and restore it with the other deps it restores (the invariant is that this test's assertions describe setup without a run memory).

Seam: US-003/US-004 `createRunMemory` → US-006 `setupRun`: entry point `setupRun` with a stubbed `_runSetupDeps.createRunMemory`; asserted through the options the stubbed `_runSetupDeps.createRuntime` receives.

**Scope** — In: run-setup.ts imports/dependency seam/config-before-memory sequence/guards/conditional runtime option, new run-setup-memory.test.ts and the authorized lifecycle fixture isolation above. Out: runtime's close implementation (US-005), run-memory composition and disable/error handling internals (US-003/US-004), prompt injection (US-007). No memory in pipeline mode or dry runs. No bot/plan changes, new permission handling or runner summary/status/footer changes. Do not stub memory globally in runner integration/e2e tests.

**Interface** — Existing setupRun API remains unchanged. The new dependency has the existing exported signature:
```ts
export async function createRunMemory(input: CreateRunMemoryInput): Promise<RunMemory | undefined>;
```
`_runSetupDeps` gains `createRunMemory`. Use the original run config for memory creation and workflow detection; pass the resolved runtimeConfig to createRuntime as shown.

Testing: drive the real setupRun with restored dependency seams, capture the real config/workdir/logger and runtime options, and record call order. Verify guards using both workflow/pipeline mode and dry-run input. Capture a logger from the run logger singleton rather than introducing a new logger instance.

userStories.title: Workflow steps put fresh memory in prompts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Read the run's fresh memory index once per generated brief/fix/review prompt and forward it to the appropriate builder.

**Motivation** — What an earlier chat or run worked out (a test command that needs a container, a review ruling, a reason a fix was reverted) is in the memory mirror, but no run session sees it, and a run session cannot save what the next one would need.

**Approach** — Callers

Each caller reads `runtime.memory` from the call context it already holds and awaits `index()` once per prompt it builds:

- `writeBrief(sc)` (`src/workflow/brief.ts`): `memoryIndex` = `await sc.callCtx.runtime.memory?.index()`.
- `runBranchFix(fc, input)` (`src/workflow/branch-fix.ts`): awaits `fc.callCtx.runtime.memory?.index()` before building the prompt and passes it to `promptFor`, which hands it to `buildWorkflowCiRepairPrompt` or `buildWorkflowBranchFixPrompt`. An explicit `input.prompt` (the bot fix path) is used as given and `index()` is not called.
- `runBranchReview(fc, input)` (`src/workflow/branch-review.ts:102`): passes `memoryIndex` the same way.

Bot review and bot fix create their runtime without a run memory, so `runtime.memory` is absent there and their prompts are unchanged.

The design document (section 6.6 and 6.8) was written in pipeline-mode vocabulary: a `ContextElement` emitted by `buildContext()` for the stages listed in `memory.stages`. Pipeline mode is frozen, and workflow mode, the `nax run` default, does not use `buildContext()`: each workflow agent session gets a prompt from its own builder, and the implementer reads a brief file written by `writeBrief` (`src/workflow/brief.ts`). So this feature delivers memory through those builders and replaces the per-stage list with one switch:

| Workflow session | Op stage | Memory it gets |
|---|---|---|
| Implementer (`wf-implementer`), including its fix / continue turns | `run` | index in the brief + the four `nax-memory` tools |
| Story review (`wf-story-review`) | `review` | the brief it already reads (no tools) |
| Branch fix (`wf-branch-fix`) and final-gate repair (`wf-repair`) | `run` | index in the prompt + tools |
| CI repair (`wf-repair` with `ciRepair`) | `run` | index in the prompt + tools |
| Whole-branch review (`wf-branch-review`) | `review` | read-only reference section (no tools) |
| Re-reviews, advisor | `review` | nothing |

The tools attach by provider stage: the run memory's provider declares `stages: ["run"]`, and the existing stage filter (`providerAttachesTo`, `packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-types.ts:71`, reached through `resolveProviderContribution` with the op's `pipelineStage`) keeps it off every `review`-stage session. No session-role list is added. Tool wiring belongs to US-003/US-004/US-005; this story only carries index text.

`src/workflow/brief.ts` — `writeBrief` awaits `sc.callCtx.runtime.memory?.index()` and passes `memoryIndex` to `buildWorkflowBrief` when defined.
`src/workflow/branch-fix.ts` — `runBranchFix` awaits `fc.callCtx.runtime.memory?.index()` when `input.prompt` is undefined and passes it to `promptFor`, which forwards it to the CI repair or branch fix builder.
`src/workflow/branch-review.ts` — `runBranchReview` awaits `fc.callCtx.runtime.memory?.index()` and passes `memoryIndex` to `buildWorkflowBranchReviewPrompt`.

Seam: US-002 builder `memoryIndex` inputs + US-005 `NaxRuntime.memory` → US-007: entry points `writeBrief`, `runBranchFix` and `runBranchReview`, with a call context whose `runtime.memory` is a fake `RunMemory`; asserted through the brief file and the prompt the stubbed `_workflowDeps.callOp` receives.

**Scope** — In: workflow/brief.ts, workflow/branch-fix.ts, workflow/branch-review.ts and new workflow-memory-prompts.test.ts. Out: implementing builders (US-002), creating/closing run memory and provider exposure (US-003 through US-006). No pipeline buildContext changes, bot/plan enablement, story or branch re-review/advisor memory, read-only review tools, session-specific adaptation of tool references, or extra sync. The story reviewer continues reading the implementer brief unchanged.

**Interface** — `promptFor(fc, input)` (`src/workflow/branch-fix.ts`, file-local). Target: `promptFor(fc, input, memoryIndex?: string)`. Existing caller APIs remain unchanged:
```ts
export async function writeBrief(sc: StepContext): Promise<void>
export async function runBranchFix(fc: BranchStepContext, input: BranchFixInput): Promise<BranchFixOutcome>
```
The existing optional `RunMemory.index(): Promise<string | undefined>` and builder `memoryIndex?: string` fields are the only new seam. Check `input.prompt !== undefined`, not truthiness: an explicit empty prompt is an override too. Preserve sessionScope, operation choice, timeout handling and leftover commit behavior.

Testing: use existing makeStepContext/makeFeatureContext/makeMockCallContext/makeScriptedCallOp helpers, a fake RunMemory and restored _workflowDeps. Assert actual brief file text and the exact prompt sent to callOp, including CI repair prefix and untouched explicit overrides; do not merely assert builder calls. No dependency on setup story US-006 is needed to test these caller seams.
acceptanceCriteria: writeBrief(sc) with sc.callCtx.runtime.memory a fake run memory whose index() resolves "INDEX-LINE" writes a brief file containing memorySectionOf("INDEX-LINE").
writeBrief(sc) with no sc.callCtx.runtime.memory writes a brief with no ## Memory heading.
writeBrief(sc) with a fake run memory whose index() resolves undefined writes a brief with no ## Memory heading.
runBranchFix(fc, { findings }) with fc.callCtx.runtime.memory a fake run memory whose index() resolves "INDEX-LINE" sends _workflowDeps.callOp a prompt containing memorySectionOf("INDEX-LINE").

runBranchFix(fc, { findings, kind: "repair", ciRepair: { round: 1 } }) with the same fake run memory sends _workflowDeps.callOp a prompt that starts with You are repairing the CI of and contains memorySectionOf("INDEX-LINE").
runBranchFix(fc, { findings, prompt: "OWN PROMPT" }) with the same fake run memory sends _workflowDeps.callOp the prompt "OWN PROMPT" unchanged.
runBranchFix(fc, { findings, prompt: "OWN PROMPT" }) does not call the fake run memory's index().
runBranchFix(fc, { findings }) with no fc.callCtx.runtime.memory sends _workflowDeps.callOp a prompt with no ## Memory heading.

runBranchReview(fc, input) with fc.callCtx.runtime.memory a fake run memory whose index() resolves "INDEX-LINE" sends _workflowDeps.callOp a prompt containing buildMemoryReferenceSection("INDEX-LINE").
runBranchReview(fc, input) with no fc.callCtx.runtime.memory sends _workflowDeps.callOp a prompt with no ## Memory heading.

routing.reasoning: Three established workflow callers await an optional index and pass text to existing builders; callOp/brief fixtures already expose the results, and no tool grants, session lifecycle or security controls change in this prompt-data wiring story.

suggestedCriteria: When writeBrief, a generated runBranchFix prompt or runBranchReview builds one prompt, the fake run memory's index is called exactly once for that prompt.
When a later writeBrief call receives a changed index result, its brief contains the later index rather than the earlier one.
runBranchFix(fc, { findings, prompt: "" }) forwards an empty prompt unchanged without calling memory.index.
runBranchFix(fc, { findings, kind: "repair" }) without ciRepair sends the branch-fix prompt containing the memory tool section.
When a run memory's guarded index returns undefined after a render failure, generated branch-fix, CI-repair and branch-review prompts contain no ## Memory heading.
When runBranchReview receives memory text, its dispatched prompt contains no nax-memory__get tool reference.

analysis:
Feature context and discovery: this is an additive enhancement to the existing memory-chat/memory-store work, not a new memory implementation. All seven implementation stories are confined to packages/nax; packages/nax-agent is read-only integration context. The execution repository is /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/nax/repos/nax. The codebase-memory MCP server/tools were unavailable in this environment, so discovery used direct Read, Grep and Glob. Findings below are verified against the present source; no implementation code or tests were run while drafting. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md before implementation: its execution-mode section identifies workflow as the default and pipeline as frozen, and its quick reference specifies a 600-line hard source cap, type-only imports, barrel APIs, dependency seams and permission resolution. Follow packages/nax/AGENTS.md and the applicable canonical .nax/rules files; use Bun APIs and bun:test in nax, shared @test/helpers, and restore mutable _deps after every test. Never change generated agent instruction files or package versions for this feature.

US-001/config: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-memory.ts:24 defines the strict MemoryConfigSchema with enabled/provider/writeMode/indexBytes/askOnSave; memoryConfigOf at :44 returns an existing typed block unchanged or parses schema defaults when absent. packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-memory.ts:11 is the hand-written MemoryConfig interface; NaxConfig.memory is optional, so new production reads must use memoryConfigOf. Add inRun with default true and a boolean runtime type; do not implement memory.stages or accept koda. The schema's opening comment currently anticipates a future stages key and should not be treated as permission to add that key. packages/nax/src/cli/config-descriptions.ts:454-461 holds the memory descriptions. packages/nax/test/unit/config/schemas-memory.test.ts:14 holds DEFAULT_MEMORY, :76-86 a configured closed literal and exact round-trip assertion, and :94 the descriptions table. Both literals must gain inRun, true for defaults and false for the configured block, preserving the existing exact equality invariants rather than loosening tests. Existing serialized configuration requires no migration: parsing supplies true; hand-authored complete MemoryConfig fixtures must include the new required member. Chat continues ignoring inRun.

US-002/prompts: packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/memory-builder.ts:13 defines the four-tool usage instructions, :34 buildMemorySection and :39 memorySectionOf; reuse the existing tool section unchanged and add a distinct fixed read-only reference section. packages/nax/src/prompts/index.ts:77 currently exports only buildMemorySection/buildMemoryToolInstructions from that module; add both reference helpers and memorySectionOf to that barrel. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-implementer-builder.ts:18 defines WorkflowBriefInput and :67 buildWorkflowBrief; the rules index and feature context are adjacent at :95-96, the exact insertion point for memory. The later project-context override and constitution order must remain intact. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts:14 defines BranchReviewPromptInput, :103 builds the whole-branch review, and :190 builds branch fix. Only the whole-branch reviewer gets the read-only reference section; do not change the re-review builder in the same file. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-ci-repair-builder.ts:28 builds the CI repair prompt; append memory after REPAIR_VERIFICATION_RULE and before WORKFLOW_REPLY_CONTRACT, not inside its How to work list. These pure builders must produce byte-identical prior output for absent or empty memoryIndex, avoiding extra whitespace, heading changes or moved contracts. Existing relevant tests are test/unit/prompts/builders/memory-builder.test.ts:7, workflow-builder.test.ts, workflow-builder-chain.test.ts, workflow-implementer-builder.test.ts and test/unit/workflow/brief-rules-index.test.ts:38. Extend existing builder tests and section-order assertions; US-002 creates no new production module and must not acquire a memory host itself.

US-003/US-004/memory composition: packages/nax/src/memory/host.ts:89 defines MemoryHost, :109 CreateMemoryHostInput, and :355 createMemoryHost; the latter returns null before mirror resolution if enabled is false. Its returned object is a concrete composition of own members, so a counting view can preserve every member while replacing only save. The host reads notes and renders the index anew, and save/forget/source stamping already live behind this API; do not reimplement store validation, sync policy or note serialization. packages/nax/src/memory/tool-provider.ts:316 builds get/search/save/forget in that order, and :354 returns the static nax-memory provider with stages ["*"]. Build a new per-run provider object overriding stages to ["run"] without mutating the shared factory or chat provider behavior. Its answer wrapper at :245 catches tool failures and returns the existing feature-2 error response. The counting wrapper increments only after a fulfilled host.save result, counts pending as a subset of saved, and leaves rejected saves and forgets uncounted. packages/nax/src/chat/host-memory.ts:65 shows guarded sync using errorMessage from @nathapp/nax-agent/internal, and :96 guarded rendering; reuse the error-reporting convention, not chat's prepare-per-open sync lifecycle. Run memory must sync only once at creation and once on its first close, while index always rerenders without syncing. Run warning/summary data use storyId _run and the logger supplied by setup. Expected sync statuses are results, not exceptions, and must not generate new run warnings. packages/nax/src/memory/index.ts:10-16 is the required public barrel. Existing memory unit suites include host.test.ts, host-index.test.ts, host-writes.test.ts, tool-provider.test.ts and tool-provider-writes.test.ts. Create test/unit/memory/run-memory.test.ts in US-003 and extend it in US-004; include a real temporary-directory host/provider seam, plus fake host failures and counter tests. US-003 deliberately exposes the final interface with zero counters and a no-op close; US-004 completes behavior before runtime integration. Guard close before its await so overlapping calls cannot double-sync or double-log.

Provider architecture and permissions: packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-types.ts:35 defines ToolProvider including readonly stages and :71 providerAttachesTo already implements stage matching. packages/nax-agent/src/tools/provider-adapt.ts:26 adapts provider tools directly to host callbacks with no file-sandbox path scope. packages/nax/src/operations/call-run-options.ts:41-58 forwards runtime providers before call-local providers, and :93 passes pipelineStage; no dispatch changes are needed. packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-implement.ts:51 declares stage run, and workflow-repair.ts:27 spreads workflowBranchFixOp, retaining its run stage. Existing provider contribution filtering, grants and capability support must remain authoritative; never add a session-role allowlist, permission bypass, new read-only tools or in-run ask flow. Review operations get no run-memory tools; the story reviewer still reads the unchanged implementer brief protocol naming get/search. Routing audit: keep strict three-session-tdd for US-003 and US-005, which establish stage-restricted tool exposure and integrate it with runtime/session-resource teardown. US-004 only wraps existing host writes for counting and idempotent close, US-006 only composes an optional resource through existing setup seams, and US-007 only forwards prompt text: these are medium, tdd-simple changes without new access-control or session-lifecycle policy. US-001/US-002 are medium, tdd-simple config/pure rendering changes. Do not infer security-critical implementation merely because a prompt is later read by an agent. packages/nax/src/execution/workflow-parallel.ts:6 clamps a requested workflow parallel count to 0; workflow does not need an outbox-only stage architecture. Host save writes the local mirror immediately.

US-005/runtime: packages/nax/src/runtime/index.ts is exactly 597 lines in this checkout; NaxRuntime starts at :155, toolProviders at :284, CreateRuntimeOptions at :294, createRuntime at :343 and close at :542. Move CreateRuntimeOptions with all doc comments to new runtime/runtime-options.ts before adding memory; keep its barrel re-export so existing callers and tests do not change imports. Existing source search finds the declaration and factory signature only, while test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-command-interceptor.test.ts:24 already imports the type from @/runtime. Both modules must import RunMemory as a type only using relative ../memory, preventing runtime-to-memory runtime graph cycles. packages/nax/src/runtime/run-tool-providers.ts:6 implements MCP-then-optional-skills ordering; append memory after the result, preserving the original provider list when no memory was supplied. Return a conditional memory property rather than memory: undefined, since callers and tests assert key absence. close already has a closed flag before teardown, but mcpPool.close at :563 can reject before flush/drain; enclose the rest of teardown in try/finally and await memory.close in finally so teardown failure cannot skip sync. Preserve existing teardown errors rather than swallowing them: memory.close is guaranteed nonthrowing. Also preserve abort, listener cleanup, manager reset/close, MCP rollup, residual spend and all audit drains. packages/nax/test/unit/runtime/runtime-skills-provider.test.ts:21-49 pins exact provider ids/order and :79 tests real dispatch forwarding; extend those invariants in new runtime-memory.test.ts, including deferred close and rejecting MCP teardown. Verification includes typecheck, file-size <=600 and import-cycle gates, not acceptance criteria about gate success.

US-006/setup: packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup.ts is 557 lines. _runSetupDeps at :70 has createRuntime and catalog/lock seams; runtimeConfigFor at :95 may await catalog MCP resolution and reject. setup currently evaluates it inline in createRuntime at :263. Resolve it first, then conditionally createRunMemory from the ORIGINAL config, absolute workdir and getLogger(), then supply the resolved runtimeConfig plus conditional memory option to the existing factory. This avoids creating memory before a failing config resolution. Dry-run and pipeline never call the memory seam; memory.inRun/disabled handling stays inside createRunMemory rather than duplicating configuration rules in setup. Import getLogger alongside existing getSafeLogger and isWorkflowMode from the config barrel. CLI logger setup precedes this lifecycle; use the run's logger, not an ad hoc instance. No new lifecycle owner is needed: runner.ts:486 awaits runtime.close on exit, and run-setup.ts:548 calls it in failure cleanup (also :353 for signal cleanup). A synchronous createRuntime throw remains the acknowledged existing resource gap; the mirror needs no extra resource finalizer. New run-setup-memory.test.ts observes the arguments/order of stubbed _runSetupDeps.createRunMemory/createRuntime rather than private locals. test/unit/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-command-interceptor.test.ts:42 uses withDepsRestore and :62 drives real setup with a mock runtime; adapt it and the other ten authorized lifecycle fixtures only to stub createRunMemory to undefined and restore it. Those authorized fixtures are gitignore-reconcile.test.ts, run-setup-approvals-seal.test.ts, run-setup-chat-asks.test.ts, run-setup-locks.test.ts, run-setup-mcp-in-run.test.ts, run-setup-no-migration.test.ts, run-setup-warnings-native-defaults.test.ts, run-setup-warnings.test.ts, run-setup.test.ts and scratchpad-wipe.test.ts, plus command-interceptor already named. Runner integration/e2e keep real memory. test/preload.ts:43 points NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR at an isolated directory, so real memory never uses the operator's home; expect one additional zero-save info line at close, not changed status/footer formats.

US-007/callers: packages/nax/src/workflow/brief.ts:103 writeBrief already concurrently resolves spec, red-base state, decisions, rules and context override before buildWorkflowBrief at :115; add one optional runtime.memory.index read per brief and forward its defined result without changing other context rules. packages/nax/src/workflow/branch-fix.ts:125 promptFor selects override, CI repair or branch fix; :142 runBranchFix currently builds synchronously inside the session callback. Read memory asynchronously once only for generated prompts, preserving an explicit input.prompt including the empty string and avoiding an index read for either override. Keep sessionScope semantics, operation selection and leftover commits intact. packages/nax/src/workflow/branch-review.ts:102 runBranchReview builds its prompt at :110 and dispatches through underReviewLimit; read memory once for this builder only, not runBranchReReview at :148. Current test/unit/workflow/branch-fix.test.ts:22 uses makeFeatureContext/makeScriptedCallOp with _workflowDeps restoration and :105 already tests both nonempty and empty explicit overrides; brief-rules-index.test.ts:85 uses makeStepContext/makeMockCallContext and a real temporary brief file. Reuse these helpers in new workflow-memory-prompts.test.ts, asserting actual written brief content and prompts observed by callOp, not merely that a builder stub was called. US-007 depends on US-002 and US-005, not US-006: a fake runtime.memory is sufficient to verify this seam.

Compatibility, risk and delivery: no storage migration, nax-agent API change, new dependency, release/version change or cross-package edit is needed. Config defaults enable workflow-run memory; inRun false opts runs out without altering chat. Main regressions to protect are exact no-memory prompt text, strict unknown config rejection, type-complete memory fixtures, provider ordering and review-stage exclusion, error-to-warning mapping, save counts after rejection, duplicate/concurrent close, sync in runtime finally, setup config-before-memory ordering, original config versus catalog-enriched runtime config, override prompts (including empty string), and unintended disk IO in mocked setup unit fixtures. Every explicit acceptance criterion stays with its binding story. Failure handling maps to US-003 (switch/master disable, host/start-sync/render failures), US-004 (rejected tools/end-sync/summary), US-005 (runtime close despite memory sync failure) and US-006 (dry-run/pipeline). Extra hardening cases not explicitly required are suggestedCriteria, not new mandatory acceptance criteria. Deliver dependency order US-001 -> US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005 -> US-006, with independent US-002 and then US-007 after US-002/US-005. Use targeted package-relative bun test paths during TDD, never bare bun test or bun run nax; the pipeline handles typecheck/lint/full tests, and coverage is not to be run inside NAX_SANDBOXED=1. No tests or quality gates have been executed for this planning-only artifact.

Refine-pass self-audit: re-read the on-disk spec and current config, host/tool-provider, runtime teardown, setup and three workflow caller implementations. Enumerated and retained all 83 explicitly listed spec ACs in their binding stories and original order: US-001 1-6, US-002 1-18, US-003 1-19, US-004 1-13, US-005 1-10, US-006 1-7, US-007 1-10. Existing extra failure-table assertions remain after those originals (US-003 #20, US-004 #14, US-005 #11), totaling 86 mandatory assertions; none of the originals were demoted to suggestions. Preserved regression qualifiers including unknown-key rejection still failing, two calls/two renders, real-host tool order, same forwarded note fields, twice-total sync including start, provider ids as before, and explicit prompt unchanged. The type-import AC now also names observable runtime.memory identity while retaining its compile/run contract. Every story already contains a negative-path AC: invalid config (001), absent/empty prompt index (002), host/sync/render rejection (003), rejected save/end-sync (004), rejecting MCP teardown (005), dry-run/pipeline guards (006), unavailable index (007). All 14 feature-level exclusions remain verbatim; there is no story-local exclusion to hoist. Every spec-recommended context file is present within the five-file cap, every expected output belongs to its creating story, and the seven workdirs and dependency arrays remain exactly binding. Removed an accidental suggestion that bots could opt into memory; clarified complete resolved-config/save-result fixtures and model-input versus MemoryNoteWrite flow to match the actual interfaces. Reduced routing for standard counter/setup/prompt wiring without weakening stage-exposure/runtime-teardown isolation. Additional behavioral hardening remains suggestedCriteria rather than newly invented mandatory requirements.
outOfScope: Pipeline mode (`execution.mode: "pipeline"`, frozen) gets no memory: no `ContextElement` of type `memory`, no tools, no index; `buildContext()` is unchanged.
The design's `memory.stages` list is not built; `memory.inRun` is the only run switch and the tools always attach to `run`-stage sessions only.
Bot review and bot fix (`nax bot review`, `nax bot fix`) get no memory index or tools; their runtime is created without a run memory.
`nax plan` gets no memory index or tools.
Story re-reviews, branch re-reviews and the advisor get no memory section.
Review-stage sessions get no read-only memory tools (`get` / `search` without `save` / `forget`); the whole-branch reviewer sees only the index lines.
The story reviewer reads the implementer's brief, whose memory section names `nax-memory__get` and `nax-memory__search`; the reviewer has no memory tools and nothing is changed for it.

The memory section is injected whenever a run memory exists, even into a session the memory tools did not attach to (the `safe` profile, a `scoped` profile without `Mcp(nax-memory__*)` grants, an agent that cannot take provider tools); the section's tool line is not adapted per session.
No sync runs between stories or mid-session; the index is re-rendered from the mirror for each prompt, and saves reach the mirror immediately through the `local` provider.

No new permission handling: memory tools follow the existing provider scope, so under the `safe` permission profile they are not attached, and under `scoped` they need `Mcp(nax-memory__*)` grants; memory tools never ask inside a run.

A run launched from a separate git worktree uses that worktree's own mirror (the mirror is keyed by the realpath of the repo root, feature 2); sharing one mirror across worktrees of one repository is not built.
The memory summary is a log line at runtime close; it is not added to the `Workflow summary` line, the headless footer, `status.json` or the PR body.
The koda provider and the generic MCP provider are features 3 and 5; `memory.provider` still accepts only `local`.
